findings.title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet raises error
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the paginator slices the queryset with a negative start index (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError` ("Negative indexing is not supported"). Any request whose cursor has a negative offset therefore gets an unhandled exception and a 500 response. The code comment saying the ORM "properly handles negative slicing automatically" is wrong.

findings.title: BasePaginator passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps only next cursors. A user-supplied prev cursor such as `1:-5:1` slices the queryset with a negative index, which raises an error and returns a 500. This affects every BasePaginator subclass across the API, not only the new audit-log path.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime keys
findings.body: `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the raw attribute value, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw number. The audit-log endpoint orders this paginator by `-datetime`, so `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError` whenever there are results. Cursor values would also be compared against the datetime column as plain numbers, which is wrong. The optimized path fails for any non-empty result set; it should use the DateTimePaginator conversion logic.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError when member is None
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated even when the requester has no membership, for example a superuser or staff user accessing the org, in which case `member` can be None. The `or` short-circuits only when `is_superuser` is true, so other non-member users with audit access (such as staff) crash with `AttributeError` before the check completes.

findings.title: Comments claim negative offsets reach data beyond pagination bounds
findings.body: The feature is described as allowing "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", with a claim that this is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level. Offsets come straight from an untrusted cursor and the bounds checks are deliberately removed. Even though the queryset is org-filtered, this is an unvalidated input path with no tests. The offset should be validated, and a BadPaginationError raised for negative values, as other paginators already do.

findings.title: No tests for new paginator or endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, a new endpoint branch, and changes BasePaginator offset handling, but includes no tests. The datetime-key crash and the negative-slice errors would have been caught by basic tests.
